title: Enhancing analytical photon transport in turbid media through physics-guided neural network corrections
abstract: arXiv:2610.26917v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Analytical methods provide rapid and computationally efficient predictions of light transport in turbid media, making them attractive for real-time and inverse applications. However, their accuracy is limited by the approximations and assumptions used to obtain tractable solutions. On the other hand, Monte Carlo (MC) simulation is widely regarded as the "gold standard" for modeling light transport in turbid media, but its high computational cost limits its use in applications requiring repeated forward evaluations. Here, we introduce a physics-guided residual learning framework that combines the computational efficiency of analytical modeling with the accuracy of MC simulation. As a representative case study, we consider the diffusion approximation (DA), which can exhibit systematic errors under relatively strong absorption, weak scattering, and imperfect boundary treatment. tldr: 本文提出一种物理引导的残差学习框架，利用神经网络修正扩散近似等解析模型的系统性误差，在保持计算效率的同时达到接近蒙特卡洛模拟的光子传输预测精度。
